newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe says govt saved Foncier, no funds.
newsitem.headline: Juppe says govt saved Foncier, no funds.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Thursday troubled bank Credit Foncier would have had to file for bankruptcy if the government had not acted, but that a state recapitalisation was not on offer.
"Credit Foncier's losses are the result of misadventure in property investments which were carried out between 1990 and 1993 under the preceding team," Juppe told the Senate.
"If we had not done what we have done in the past year Credit Foncier would have had to file for bankruptcy," he said.
He recalled that the government had stood in to guarantee the bonds Credit Foncier had issued and then organised a buyout of the group by state-owned bank Caisse de Depots.

That buyout was the first step of a plan unveiled by Finance Minister Jean Arthuis in July, with the second stage involving spinning off the home loans business to rival, cooperatively run Credit Immobilier, and winding down the rest over time.

"Is it conceivable to ask taxpayers for the eight billion francs needed to soak up those losses and recapitalise Credit Foncier? I don't think so, I don't think this is possible," Juppe told the upper house of parliament.

Staff were occupying the headquarters for a seventh day on Thursday as union negotiators sought guarantees from mediator Philippe Rouvillois that the Arthuis plan be halted pending the search for another solution.

"Today the public authorities have their backs to the wall," said union negotiator Patrick Kronenbitter of the CFDT union on the way into talks with Rouvillois. "If they hold fast they risk setting the whole country alight," he added.

Arthuis said in the Senate Credit Foncier could not survive alone, that Credit Immobilier was the only one to show interest and that this had to be where a solution was found as long as there was no other suitor.
But he said there was no tight deadline and no obsession with a single option.
